chapter: Algiers parades and the wider city
title: White brass bands in Algiers and the first band he saw
summary: The first bands he saw as a boy were white ones, playing at funerals; Papa Lane is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, I was going to ask some more about the parades over on this side of the river. Did they ever have many parades here?

Well, here at Sesto, Sesto's organization, this band and music, you know. In the old days? Oh, in the old days, yeah. Well, I'll tell you, you take it in the old days. Well, I'll tell you real facts. The white people used to use bands for fuming too. In the old days. That's what I heard of them. Yeah. Now, they're the first one I seen playing when I was a youngster. There was a white band playing fuming. Oh, it was a white band. Yeah, that's the first band I seen before I saw color.
Used to bear right there in that cemetery right there. Cali Cemetery. Used to go to the Mike Down Cemetery.
Yeah, no. But, you know, it seemed like the color people picked it up.
But, they're the first one I saw. I might have seen Papa Lane's band there.

There was one old time musician Papa Lane, he said he was playing especially in Gretna, I think the David Crockett Fire department. Yeah, yeah, yeah. I think they'd even buried with music and one of their members had done. Yeah, yeah. Well, they had the, they had the. Some of those clubs and stuff like that.

Yeah. Then they had a, well, I forget his name. He lived down here on Alex Street. I forget his name. They had a brass band too. Street band, you know. He's dead too now. I forget his name now. But, they're the first one I saw playing like that. Finally after I saw, you know, color.
How old would you be then when you saw that?
Oh, gee, when I saw that I was running about eight years of age. That's been a long time. I'm going on six to eight. I ran about eight or nine years of age. Yeah. They're the first one I saw.
